newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, demand thin.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, demand thin.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Tuesday, with sharp falls in Malaysia keeping buyers sidelined, traders said.

They said olein was quoted at 1,410-15 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were also heard at 1,405 rupiah. Crude palm oil was offered at 1,170 rupiah/kg in the North Sumatran city of Medan, but buyers were at 1,160-65.

"The market was slow, due in part to the declines in Malaysia," one trader said. "Buyers are also not keen on taking positions because of the rupiah's decline against the dollar. They are waiting to see if the rupiah will strengthen."
The rupiah has regained some strength against the U.S. dollar after speculative offshore attacks plunged the currency to a historic low a week ago, but remains fragile.

Traders also said players were looking to the export market because of premium prices. "There is a good margin in exporting crude palm oil at the moment, and I think players will be more keen on exporting," one trader said.

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Indra left for Malaysia on Sunday with 7,350 tonnes of crude palm oil, while the MT Mando will leave for Pasir Gudang, Malaysia, on Tuesday with 12,510 tonnes of crude palm oil.
The MT Jollnd will leave for Dumai on Wednesday with 22,500 tonnes of palm oil.
